assessment: The response is a strong, numerically grounded recommendation: it correctly derives the $95 free-shipping threshold from the given economics, shows the 15% discount requires an implausible 55.6% order lift, and proposes a sensible contribution-per-visitor A/B test. Its main weaknesses are experimental rigor (undefined confidence level, no sample-size/power analysis, and stopping 'once significance is reached' which invites peeking bias) and incomplete risk coverage (variable shipping costs, returns, customer conditioning, seasonality). Four of five judges converged closely on scores of 6-9, with the Google judge as a clear positive outlier at 10 across all criteria.
judge_agreement: Four judges (anthropic, openai, deepseek, qwen) agreed tightly: high specificity (6-9), solid practicality (6-7), and moderate risk awareness (5-7), all converging on the same critiques around 'reasonable confidence', sample size, and peeking bias. The Google judge was a stark outlier, awarding perfect 10s and explicitly stating 'None needed' for improvements on every criterion, which contradicts the specific, well-evidenced gaps identified by the rest of the panel. No judge identified rule or tool errors.
